summary: The study focuses on the kinetic modeling of TiN film growth in atomic layer deposition (ALD) using tetrakis(dimethylamido)titanium and ammonia as precursors. The process involves alternating pulses of the precursors at 180 °C, with the growth rate influenced by adsorption and readsorption mechanisms. The maximum film growth rate was found to be up to 2 ML/cycle, depending on the volume reduction of the reactants.
evidence: In our experiments of TiN-ALD on SiO2/Si substrates, two reactant gases, tetrakis(dimethylamido)-titanium (TDMAT) and NH3 were alternately supplied into the reaction chamber at the deposition temperature of 180 °C. Thus, one deposition cycle is composed of a sequential supply of TDMAT vapor pulse, purge gas pulse, NH3 gas pulse and purge gas pulse. The values of partial pressure for TDMAT and for NH3 were about 4 and 44 Pa, respectively. ALD takes place in a self-limiting layer-by-layer manner, and it is considered that 1 at. ML in one deposition cycle (ML/cycle) can be obtained as the maximum film growth rate in an ideal case. However, it has been reported that the growth rate was over 1 ML/deposition cycle in binary compound systems including our experimental results of the TiN system. Hence, in this proposed model, we introduce the 'readsorption' concept as follows. When the TDMAT vapor pulse is injected into the reaction chamber in an arbitrary kth deposition cycle, TDMAT molecules adsorb onto the film surface, and then instantly react with the previously readsorbed NH3 molecules, which have adsorbed on the film surface during the NH3 gas pulse in the (k-1)th deposition cycle, to form a new TiN atomic layer. Also, during this TDMAT vapor pulse, other TDMAT molecules will have chances to readsorb onto both the newly formed TiN atomic layer and newly exposed TiN film surface, which becomes the outermost surface again by the volume reduction of NH molecules forming the new TiN atomic layer. By assuming the proposed readsorptions during each pulse of the TDMAT and the NH3 gas, the maximum TiN film thickness that can be deposited in one deposition cycle can be increased up to 2 ML/cycle.
